evidence.r1: The entire Active alerts content list sits on a frosted glass sidebar.
evidence.r2: The alert cards and selected-vehicle action buttons read as ordinary fills inside or beside the glass surfaces.
evidence.r3: Three top bars, a zoom bar, a large alert sidebar and a selected-vehicle platter make a crowded glass layer.
evidence.r4: The top controls, sidebar and vehicle platter share a milky regular-glass appearance.
evidence.r5: No clear-glass variant is visible over the map; the floating surfaces are cloudy and pale.
evidence.r6: The status-filter controls carry several coloured status marks rather than reserving colour for one primary background.
evidence.r7: The normal sidebar and vehicle platter pick up map colour and detail diffusely through their material.
evidence.r8: The bars and alert cards have fixed rounded corners and the small markers have rounded-rectangle outlines.
evidence.r9: The alert cards nearly fill the sidebar width but their upper corner arcs do not share the sidebar corner centres.
evidence.r10: The bordered Call and Log to incident text buttons are rounded rectangles rather than capsules.
evidence.r11: Routes, statuses and search occupy three distinct top groups with related options grouped together.
evidence.r12: The route and status buttons are text groups, while the zoom icons have their own separate glass strip.
evidence.r13: The route and status material spans each complete filter strip rather than the individual labels.
evidence.r14: Filter choices share continuous bars, and the search and zoom controls have deliberate separate spacing.
evidence.r15: Alert cards clip beneath the Active alerts header and at the sidebar bottom without a visible scroll-edge treatment.
evidence.r16: The street grid, routes and river provide varied content behind the glass controls.
evidence.r17: Vehicles and route lines run beneath the resting alert sidebar and the selected-vehicle platter.
evidence.r18: The pale map controls are readable, but no dark capture establishes both-mode contrast ratios.
evidence.r19: The reduced-transparency sidebar is usable, but increased-contrast and reduced-motion states are not demonstrated.
evidence.r20: The map reaches all window edges and continues behind the top controls and sidebar.
evidence.r21: Route lines and vehicle markers disappear beneath the sidebar without a visible safe-area or background-extension equivalent.
evidence.r22: The floating bars show material edges without a separate custom backing layer.
evidence.r23: The selected-vehicle still shows placement but no morph or pointer-local press animation.
evidence.r24: The floating status filter contains blue, amber and red marks instead of monochrome control content.
evidence.r25: Dark route, search and vehicle-platter labels remain distinct from the pale map-derived surface colours.
